consequences: The compiler runway must lower accepted source, population, and operation plans into one exact frontend-neutral KnowledgeChangeSet before governed domain-state admission.
The protocol machine may produce, validate, or admit exact change-set and receipt data, but only an identified projector folding verified ledger history may derive the accepted temporal graph.
Production KnowledgeGraph, staging, projection, Assent, and protocol cutovers inherit the KnowledgeChangeSet boundary through the Small Shop vertical dependency.
Persisted structural candidates remain independently useful but cannot claim governed or accepted Malleus knowledge without semantic-history admission.
constraints: KnowledgeChangeSet is the one immutable frontend-neutral domain-state change unit and binds contract, source and evidence closure, base ledger and state identity, ordered operations, valid time, supersession, local dependencies, and digest.
Proposal, checks, review, decision, and application remain separate lifecycle records and reference the same immutable change-set identity.
There is one authoritative ordered semantic and protocol ledger and one replay-derived accepted temporal graph with no independent accepted-state write path.
Governed initial state is an empty graph plus a completely retained genesis change set or identified genesis set; a nonempty external base cannot be unexplained accepted knowledge.
PopulationPlan, GraphConstructionPlan, GraphRecipe expansion, and OperationDependencyPlan are derivation inputs, not another knowledge graph, ledger, state authority, or domain identity.
An ACCEPT decision event may carry failure-atomic application while preserving distinct decision and application records.
Ontology evolution later requires an explicit cross-contract KnowledgeChangeSet or migration change set.
This decision creates no runtime or ontology implementation, public wire grammar, stable API, candidate, selection, or worker ledger.
data.selected_option: One ledger admits immutable KnowledgeChangeSet values; accepted graphs are replay-only

summary: Make immutable KnowledgeChangeSet values the sole governed domain-state change unit.
why: Graph planning, semantic history, and accepted projection previously met without one exact public state-change artifact. That gap allowed a plan, materializer, external graph base, or direct graph API to look like a second authority. The decision binds every governed change to one immutable unit admitted through one ledger and makes every accepted graph a replay-derived view, while preserving simpler structural-only adoption as an optional lower profile.
